prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in League City, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1479; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not put my name on it yet, but you can refer to me as the driver of the vehicle.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a multi-lane road in League City, Texas, in the right lane heading toward the interchange. Traffic was moderate and moving steadily.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was changing lanes to the left because I needed to get over for my exit. I checked my mirror and glanced over my shoulder, and I thought the lane was clear.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle at any point?

A: Not until it was right alongside me. I heard a loud scrape and felt my car pushed toward the right. I think the other car had been in my blind spot the whole time.

Q: Did you apply your brakes or swerve?

A: I braked a little and steered back toward my lane. I didn't go off the road, but my car was shaking and the steering felt off.

Q: How are you feeling physically now?

A: My right shoulder hurts quite a bit. I hit the seatbelt pretty hard when the car jolted, and I've had trouble lifting my arm above my head since then.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or gone to an emergency room?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that afternoon. They took X-rays and told me to follow up with an orthopedic specialist if the pain doesn't improve.

Q: Did anyone else in your vehicle get hurt?

A: No, I was alone in the car.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I want to cooperate fully and I hope we can sort out the damage to my vehicle quickly.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
